absent: Permission evaluation inside creation and deletion validators.
Security hook effects for path and inode operations.
Resolution mechanics of creation, parent lookup and directory iteration helpers.
Stale retry predicate and revalidation mechanics.
Filesystem operation implementations beyond presence check.
Mount write hold acquisition and release behavior.
Attribute change application inside timed update path.
Hash function, table sizing and RCU lifetime rules.
Shrinker accounting and list management beyond isolation callback.
System control and debug file registration lifetime effects.

findings.text: Symlink creation is split between a filename level helper that resolves a new destination and a lower helper that performs checks then delegates to filesystem code. The upper helper repeats the attempt after a delegation is resolved and after a stale indication requests revalidation. The lower helper enforces creation permission, demands filesystem support, consults security policy, negotiates directory delegations, invokes the filesystem routine, and emits a creation notification only when the operation succeeds.

Directory creation follows a similar two level shape with directory oriented lookup. The upper helper requests a creation slot, derives a masked mode for security evaluation, calls into the lower helper, then finalizes the path and retries on delegation or stale conditions. The lower helper validates creation rights, requires filesystem support, normalizes the mode for directory type, consults security policy, enforces a filesystem link ceiling, negotiates delegations, invokes filesystem code, adopts any returned alias entry, and notifies on success while releasing the creation hold on failure.

Directory removal resolves a parent and final component, rejects special trailing components with distinct failures, holds write access, starts a directory operation, checks security, and calls a lower helper. The lower helper validates deletion rights, requires filesystem support, pins the victim and serializes it, refuses mount points and kernel internal files, consults security, negotiates delegations, invokes filesystem code, then prunes descendant cache entries, marks the victim dead, blocks future mounts and detaches existing mounts before releasing serialization and emitting deletion notification on success. Delegation and stale conditions cause an outer retry.

Timestamp update validates supplied nanosecond fields, treats a dual request for current time as an untimed touch, acquires write access, builds an attribute mask distinguishing omitted fields from explicit values and current time requests, marks explicit updates distinctly from a generic touch, then serializes the target while applying the change and retries if a delegation was encountered before releasing write access.

Inode management provides initialization of a fresh structure with safe defaults, insertion and removal from a global hash, lookup by superblock plus tester predicate with careful handling of freeing and creating states, disposal of a failed new object by clearing its newness and waking waiters, and reclamation of cached objects through a shrinker that disposes a collected list.

Link and directory creation notifications combine an audit record for child creation with a filesystem event. Link notification first accounts the additional link, then audits and reports creation against the parent. Directory creation notification audits and reports a directory flavored creation event.

Small utilities cover link count maintenance with special handling when reviving from zero, one time initialization of address space structures and cache objects, defensive diagnostic dumping of mapping host and name without faulting, and paired helpers to acquire and release two non directory serializations in a stable order with a nested subclass for the second.

Early boot filesystem helpers wrap normal namespace operations with kernel internal filenames and the current working directory context. They expose symlink creation, unlink, directory creation, directory removal, timestamp update through path resolution plus timed update, and descriptor duplication by allocating an unused number and installing a reference. All are marked for initialization use.

Filesystem wide observability is registered during initialization. One entry publishes inode counters through two system control names sharing a common handler that refreshes counts before delegation to a generic integer vector handler. Another entry publishes multigrain timestamp counters through a debug file whose show routine formats four accumulated values.

Global inode hash mutation acquires the global hash spin protection before the per object spin protection, performs hashed list insertion or removal with release ordering safe primitives, then releases in reverse order. Lookup asserts expected hash protection state and uses read side critical sections with per object serialization only for state inspection and reference acquisition.

Reclaim inverts the usual list versus object lock order and therefore uses a non blocking attempt on the object lock, skipping objects that are busy. When page cache must be discarded the code marks the object as undergoing isolation while holding its lock, drops both locks to perform potentially blocking invalidation, then clears the mark under lock and wakes waiters.

Paired non directory locking orders the two inputs by address to avoid deadlock, warns if either is a directory, acquires the first with the normal primitive and the second with a nested subclass unless identical or absent, with a symmetric release. Elsewhere removal serializes the victim, timed update serializes the target around change application, and hash insertion lookup and discard coordinate through the per object spin protection and wakeups.

Creation and removal lower helpers fail with a permission style error when the parent directory does not implement the corresponding operation. Validation of creation or deletion rights and security mediation precede any delegation negotiation and any invocation of filesystem code, and notification occurs only on success.

Filename level creation and removal helpers share a retry discipline. If delegation state is reported they wait for resolution and repeat from resolution without revalidation. If a stale condition is reported they enable revalidation and repeat. Write holdings and path references are released before each retry decision.

Nanosecond validation accepts two symbolic sentinel values and otherwise requires an inclusive bounded range. Attribute construction starts from change plus modification plus access, removes access or modification when omission is requested, records explicit seconds when a concrete value is supplied, flags any timed request as an explicit time set, and uses a touch flag when no times are supplied or when both request current time.

Removal distinguishes trailing dot, dot dot and root with invalid, non empty and busy failures respectively before acquiring write access. After pinning the victim it fails busy when the target is a local mount point or flagged as a kernel internal file. On success the victim is marked dead after cache pruning and mount handling.

Directory creation normalizes the requested mode against full access plus sticky bits for directory type, evaluates security with a umask stripped variant while invoking filesystem code with the original mode value, and refuses with a link count failure when a configured filesystem maximum is non zero and already reached.

Fresh inode initialization establishes a single reference, unit link count, zeroed size block and generation state, cleared flags and state, empty operations with a failing open by default, root identity, unset write hint, null private pipe device and link pointers, empty mapping with safe allocation mask, and lock class association derived from filesystem type, while enabling extended attribute and multigrain time options according to superblock features.

A discarded new object must currently carry newness. The implementation pairs a write barrier with clearing that marker and waking waiters before releasing a reference. Reclaim skips objects with live references, with state beyond a recent reference indication, or with unshrinkable cache by dequeuing them lazily. Recently referenced objects are cleared and rotated for another pass, objects with remaining cache trigger invalidating retry, and only otherwise idle non new objects transition to freeing and move to a disposal list.

Persistent global structures include a hash mask and shift plus table pointer fixed after initialization, a cache line aligned hash spin protection, per processor totals for live and unused inodes and for multigrain timestamp activity, a slab cache pointer, a per processor last allocated number for batch allocation, and a statistics block shared by two control entries. Per inode state combines identity, link count, operation vectors, locks, mapping, dentry list, and notification and security fields initialized to neutral values.

Observability layout exposes two control names for inode totals with read only access and distinct lengths for two versus seven long values, and a debug file named for multigrain timestamps with regular file type and world readable mode. The timestamp file formats four counters in decimal separated by spaces followed by newline.

The debug file helper has two build configurations. One selects a full or short creation routine based on the static type of the operations pointer. The other unconditionally reports absence of device support.
This translation unit enables trace point definitions before including implementation headers.

Inode state evolves through markers for newness, freeing, will free, creating, isolating for reclaim, referenced, and linkable revival. Lookup waits and retries when freeing or will free is observed, fails stale when creating is observed, and reports newness based on the new marker. Isolation asserts absence of freeing will free and isolating before setting isolating, then clears it with wakeup. Revival from zero links warns unless linkable and adjusts a removal counter.

Creation and removal proceed through resolve, security check, delegation negotiation, filesystem invocation and finalize phases, with exits to retry on delegation resolution or stale revalidation, to failure propagation on validation or filesystem error, and to notification only along the success path. Timed update uses a smaller loop of lock apply unlock with delegation retry.

Diagnostic dumping of a mapping treats all pointers as potentially invalid, probing host and operations, inode number and dentry linkage, and name bytes with fault tolerant copies before logging, and emits distinct warnings for invalid mapping, missing host, invalid inode, missing alias, invalid dentry, and a final name qualified message that is explicitly marked as uncertain.

Removal hazards center on lifetime and visibility. The victim is pinned and locked before mount and kernel file checks to prevent concurrent unmount or reuse races. Cache pruning, dead marking, mount blocking and mount detachment occur while still serialized and before notification, ensuring no new lookups succeed after success is reported.

Reclaim asserts that objects selected for freeing are not new and that isolation marking is not reentered nor applied to freeing objects, and paired acquisition helpers warn when asked to treat directories as non directories. Violations indicate caller contract breaches rather than expected races.
Batch size for inode number allocation is 1024.

Control names are inode-nr with length for two long values and inode-state with length for seven long values, both read only. Debug file name is multigrain_timestamps with regular file plus read for all mode.
Valid nanosecond values are zero through 999999999 inclusive plus two symbolic sentinels for omit and now.
